per_shot.note: Segmented orange serpent is on-palette with a glowing underbelly, but at play size it is pinned behind the tripod beacon whose glare swamps it; the head and fangs are tiny and the tail clips into the wall.
Chunky faceted armour plates with an ember-lit belly seam read as low-poly house style; the head and jaw are the weakest part, and the scene light comes from the beacon rather than the creature.
Violet crystal spider throws a soft cyan pool onto the rock beside a magenta ore, a good deliberate accent against VEIL amber; at play size it is small and the biting end does not read.
Faceted crystal body and legs with a cyan crown whose glow lands on the floor and wall; it reads as a crystal spider, but there is no clear maw or teeth to sell 'ore that bites'.
Two white-hot figures shed ember sparks and pool light on the floor; eerie and clearly made of light, though they read as passive ghosts more than pursuers.
Strong bloom and floor wash with faceted head and limb forms; the core is blown out to flat white, so form and menace are lost in the brightest area.
Flock of faceted ice-cyan birds reads instantly in the beam and sits squarely in the CRYOS palette; they do not glow themselves, so outside the lamp they would vanish.
Crisp low-poly origami wings with good facet value contrast; they are lit entirely by the headlamp and give off no light of their own.

top_issues.issue: Long One is upstaged by the tripod beacon at play size
top_issues.why: The beacon's glare sits on top of the serpent's midsection and is the brightest thing in the frame, so the creature reads as a decoration on the light rather than the threat, and its own glow cannot be told apart from the beacon's.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage it away from other emissives, let its belly seam and eyes be the main light that washes the tunnel walls, and enlarge or brighten the head and jaw so the dangerous end reads first.

top_issues.issue: Rimewings emit no light of their own
top_issues.why: The direction asks for creatures lit by themselves in the dark; these are lit only by the headlamp and would be invisible outside the beam.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a faint cyan emissive edge or core to each wing and a soft cold spill onto nearby ice, keeping it dimmer than the lamp.

top_issues.issue: Mimic's threat end does not read
top_issues.why: It looks like a pretty crystal spider; nothing says 'this ore bites' at either scale.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a visible faceted maw or split-open jaw under the crown, with a hot inner glow, and make it a little larger at play size.

top_issues.issue: Kindled core is blown out to flat white
top_issues.why: The overexposed centre erases the faceted form and makes the figures read as passive, not pursuing.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Hold the core at a warm hot-white with facet shading, and give them a forward lean or a reaching pose plus a darker gap for a face so they read as hunters.

protect: Kindled as true light-bodies with ember sparks and a light pool on the floor
Mimic's cyan glow landing on the surrounding rock as a cold accent in VEIL
Rimewings' crisp faceted ice-cyan origami silhouettes
Long One's chunky plated, ember-seamed body on the VEIL palette

per_shot.note: The curling silhouette with black fangs reads, but the body is a dark unlit shape with orange edge lines and dots, floating in an empty black cavern with no rock for light to land on.
A jumble of dark boxes, orange dots, stray grey squares and black spikes; head, body and the dangerous end cannot be read.
The scene is lit nicely, but the creature is a tiny purple lump with a flat cyan cube, gives off no glow, and could be mistaken for a pickup.
Flat cyan square, purple blob, a black bar for a mouth and thin dark legs; it looks like a placeholder, with no glow and no faceting.
Two black capsules with spark particles; it reads as a missing material, not a pursuer made of light, and it casts no light.
Close up the black pills are obvious; this directly contradicts the creature's identity as made of light.
Dim dark-blue shards in the beam read as debris, not birds, and they have no glow of their own.
Loose flat triangles with no wing or body structure and no glow; they read as falling ice chips.

top_issues.why: A creature made of light that shows as unlit black pills breaks its identity and looks like a missing material.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give it emissive, faceted humanoid bodies that bloom and pool light on the floor, as in A.

top_issues.issue: No creature glows or lights its surroundings
top_issues.why: This fails 'glow that lands' and the 10-creatures reference; the creatures are dark props.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add emissive parts and local light spill on every creature, tuned to its world's hue.

top_issues.why: The segments overlap in a knot with stray grey squares, so neither the body nor the head reads.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use clean overlapping plates along a clear spine with a distinct head and jaw, and remove the debris squares.

top_issues.issue: Rimewings and Mimic read as debris or placeholders
top_issues.why: Loose triangles and flat primitives give no silhouette of a body, wing or maw.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build articulated faceted bodies: wings joined to a body for Rimewings, and a crystal carapace with legs and a maw for the Mimic.

top_issues.issue: Long One habitat is an empty void
top_issues.why: There is no nearby rock for the creature's light to land on, and black void here overrides 'black reserved for true void' depth staging.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage it in a tunnel or against rock faces that its glow can wash.

why: A's creatures are faceted, emissive and on-palette, with glow that lands. B's read as unlit placeholders: the Kindled are black capsules and the Rimewings and Mimic look like debris or primitives.
